This matches the previously documented batch-applied/retroactive termination-date pattern rather than being a new anomaly: full-calendar-month June is 72,486 (vs 72,483 in the prior run, essentially unchanged), meaning ~95% of June's terminations are now captured by day 29, with the remainder landing on day 30.

Full calendar month totals for context (uConnect): 2026-03: 8,080; 2026-04: 52,134; 2026-05: 44,676; 2026-06: 72,486; 2026-07 (partial, through 07-29): 27,495. May's full-month total (44,676) exactly equals the 05-01→05-29 MTD figure used in the baseline, confirming May's terminations were also fully captured by day 29 — same batch pattern seen for June.

Known data-shape issue, still unresolved: because June's and May's MTD-through-day-29 windows already capture ~95-100% of their full-month totals (due to batch-applied termination dates), comparing July's partial-month figure (also through day 29, with its own month-end batch presumably still to post) against these near-complete baselines will structurally understate July. This RED flag should be read with that caveat rather than as confirmed evidence of a genuine slowdown in termination processing — recommend the data team resolve the underlying batch-timing behavior so this check's day-of-month-cutoff comparison becomes reliable.
